I or T: B2 [ I or T ] to make a very strong and urgent request
B2 [ I or T ] to ask for food or money because you are poor
I: › [ I ] If a dog begs, it sits with its front legs in the air as if to ask for something.
› a polite way of saying "I am sorry" or "Could you repeat what you just said?"
（未聽清時，禮貌的說法）對不起，能否再說一遍？
› a way of showing that you are angry about something that someone has just said.
（表示生氣，感覺受到冒犯）你說什麼？再說一遍！

example: They begged for mercy.
他們乞求饒恕。
[ + obj + to infinitive ] He begged her to stay, but she simply laughed and put her bags in the car.
他求她留下來，但是她只是一笑置之，把袋子放進汽車裡。
There are more and more homeless people begging on the streets these days.
近來越來越多無家可歸的人在街上行乞。
She had to beg for money and food for her children.
她不得不為孩子們乞討金錢和食物。
He begged a loan from his boss.
他求老闆借給他一筆錢。
They have trained their dog to sit up and beg.
他們把狗訓練得會兩腿直立做乞求動作。
I beg your pardon? I hope you're not implying that I lied!
我沒聽錯吧？我希望你不是在暗示我撒謊了！

NONE: › to ask to be allowed not to do something that you are expected to do
請求不做…

example: She begged off early from the party because she was so tired.
她請求早點離開聚會，因為她太累了。

NONE: › If a statement or situation begs the question, it causes you to ask a particular question.
（說法或情況）使人想要提出問題
› to talk about something as if it were true, even though it may not be
以假定作為論據來辯論

example: Spending the summer travelling around India is a great idea, but it does beg the question of how we can afford it.
到印度去旅行過夏天當然是個好主意，但關鍵問題是我們如何能負擔得起。
To discuss the company's future begs the question of whether it has a future.
要討論這間公司的前途問題，不得不問一句：這間公司還有前途嗎？

NONE: › to do whatever is necessary to get something
（為獲得…）不擇手段

example: I'm going to get a dress for the prom, whether I have to beg, borrow, or steal one.
我要找一套舞會上穿的晚裝，不管是去討、借還是偷。

NONE: › past simple of
begin (START TO HAPPEN)
› old use to be the father of
成為…的父親
› formal to cause
引起，導致

example: In the Bible it says that Adam begat Cain and Abel.
《聖經》中說亞當生了該隱和亞伯。
Poverty begets hunger, and hunger begets crime.
貧窮導致饑餓，饑餓則導致犯罪。

NONE: › a poor person who lives by asking others for money or food
乞丐，叫花子
› UK informal a person, especially when you are expressing an opinion about something that they have done, or that has happened to them
傢夥
› to make a person or organization, etc. extremely poor
使（人或組織等）極度貧窮

example: You've won again, you lucky beggar.
你又贏了，你這個幸運的傢夥！
Those children have been running about in my rose garden again, the little beggars (= annoying people)!
那些孩子又在我的玫瑰園裡到處亂跑，真是些淘氣的小傢夥！

NONE: › to be impossible to believe or describe
非言語所能形容；難以置信

example: His cruelty beggared belief/description.
他兇殘至極，簡直令人難以形容。

NONE: › small in amount and not at all generous
少量的；貧乏的
› like a beggar in appearance, way of life, etc.
乞丐般的；赤貧的

example: The council voted to give the new project a beggarly amount of money.
委員會投票撥給這個新的專案計劃少量的資金。
a poor and beggarly people
一個赤貧的、乞丐般的民族

NONE: › said when you recognize that you must accept an offer or a situation because it is the only one available to you
要飯的哪能挑肥揀瘦；別無選擇

example: I would have preferred a house of my own rather than sharing, but beggars can't be choosers, I suppose.
我比較喜歡獨住而不是跟別人住在一起，可是我怎麼可以挑三揀四的，是吧。

I or T: A1 to start to happen or exist
A2 to start to do something
› to have something as the first part

example: What time does the concert begin?
音樂會甚麼時候開始？
The bridge was begun five years ago and the estimated cost has already doubled.
這座橋五年前開始建造，到現在為止估計成本已經增加了一倍。
The film they want to watch begins at seven.
他們要看的電影七點開場。
The meeting began promisingly, but then things started to go wrong.
會議開始時很不錯，不過後來出了問題。
I began the book six months ago, but I can't seem to finish it.
我六個月前就開始看這本書，但似乎總是看不完。
[ + -ing verb ] Jane has just begun learning to drive.
珍妮剛開始學駕駛。
If you want to learn to play a musical instrument, it might be a good idea to begin on something simple.
如果你想學一種樂器，從簡單的開始或許是個好主意。
[ + to infinitive ] After waiting for half an hour she was beginning to get angry.
等了半小時後，她開始生氣了。
I have so much to tell you, I don't know where to begin.
我有很多話要跟你說，不知從何談起。
[ + speech ] "Well," he began. "I don't quite know how to tell you this."
「唉，」他開始說，「我真是不知道該怎麽樣跟你說這件事。」

NONE: A2 a person who is starting to do something or learn something for the first time
新手，初學者

example: This judo class is for beginners only.
這個柔道課程是專為初學者開設的。

NONE: › unexpected success experienced by a person who is just starting a particular activity
新手的好運氣

example: When I won the first contest I entered, he put it down to beginner's luck.
我第一次參加比賽就勝出了，他認為這是新手的好運氣。

NONE: › a
nursery slope

C usually singular, U: A2 [ C usually singular,  U ] the first part of something or the start of something

C often plural: › [ C often plural ] the origin of something, or the place, time, or way in which something started

example: Notes on how to use this dictionary can be found at the beginning of the book.
這本詞典的使用說明在全書的開頭處。
She sat down and read the book straight through from beginning to end.
她坐下來，一口氣把書從頭到尾看完了。
I enjoyed my job at/in the beginning (= when I started it), but I'm bored with it now.
剛開始時，我很喜歡我的工作，可是現在我已經厭倦了。
The city had its beginnings in Roman times.
這座城市起源於古羅馬時代。

NONE: › go away
走開，滾

example: "Begone!" he shouted. "And never show your face again!"
「滾」他吼著說，「永遠別讓我再看見你！」

NONE: › a garden plant with brightly coloured flowers
秋海棠
› to feel unhappy because someone has something that you think they do not deserve
羡慕；嫉妒
› to feel unhappy about spending money on something or spending time doing something
抱怨，發牢騷

example: [ + two objects ] I don't begrudge him his freedom.
我並不羡慕他的自由。
They begrudged every day they had to stay with their father.
他們抱怨每天都不得不和父親在一起。
[ + -ing verb ] She begrudged paying so much for an ice cream cone.
她抱怨買個雪糕筒這樣貴。

NONE: › to persuade, attract, or interest someone, sometimes in order to deceive them
使陶醉；使著迷；哄騙

example: He was completely beguiled by her beauty.
他完全被她的美貌給迷住了。
The salesman beguiled him into buying a car he didn't want.
推銷員哄騙他買下了一輛他並不需要的汽車。

NONE: › interesting or attractive, but perhaps not to be trusted
有趣的，迷人的

example: That's a beguiling argument, but I'm not convinced by it.
那個論證很有意思，但未能把我說服。

NONE: › past participle of
begin (START TO HAPPEN)
